compiled_state.description:
## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `smart-disloyal-naga` (8386-a512-4815-4e6b), via an independent
write-safety audit of the materialized ticket-store entry. Not a root cause of 8386; a
separate defect found while proving that one.

## Problem

`<store>/tickets-<sha>/` is documented and treated as an **immutable, content-addressed**
entry (ADR 0005 D2). It is not. Every `show_ticket` read through the pinned root writes a
derived reducer cache **inside the entry**:

`reducer/_api.py:221` -> `write_cache(cache_path, ...)` with
`cache_path = os.path.join(ticket_dir, ".cache.json")` (`reducer/_cache.py:196`, published at
`:146` via `atomic_write`). A second site, `reducer/_processors.py:58`, writes the same file on
the corrupt-CREATE replay path.

**Measured on this host:** one live entry
(`tickets-00b00a6ee3e2b6c0ebb667c044eb303ccf2ba3e3`) holds **4,844 `.cache.json` files**, every
one with an mtime newer than the entry directory itself — i.e. created by reads after
materialization, not by `checkout-index`. They are gitignored on the tickets branch, so they are
absent from the committed tree and are purely post-build artifacts.

## Why it matters

1. **The immutability premise is false**, and other code is entitled to rely on it. Bug 8386's
   fix now hardlinks unchanged blobs between adjacent entries; it is safe only because
   `atomic_write` publishes by `os.replace` (`_store/fsutil.py:96`) rather than writing in
   place. That is an incidental property of one line, not an enforced invariant. If that line
   ever becomes a plain `open(path, "w")`, every entry sharing the inode is silently corrupted.
2. **It already breaks the reverify pass.** `janitor.reverify_entry` (`janitor.py:249-277`)
   records a TOFU digest over the entry's contents at first sight. Reads keep adding
   `.cache.json` files afterwards, so a baseline taken before the first read makes the entry
   look **corrupt** on the next pass and evicts it. Opt-in today (`reverify_seconds > 0`), which
   is the only reason this has not bitten.
3. It inflates the store, which is the parent bug's whole subject: ~4.8k extra files per entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reading a ticket through a pinned snapshot root does not write into the snapshot entry
      (e.g. the reducer cache is disabled, or redirected outside the entry, when the tracker
      root is a snapshot).
- [ ] A test observes the write RED (a materialized entry's file set changes after a read) and
      GREEN after the fix.
- [ ] The rename-over contract in `_store/fsutil.py` is pinned by a test, or the entry is made
      genuinely read-only, so a future in-place write cannot silently corrupt shared inodes.
- [ ] ADR 0005's immutability claim is either enforced or amended to describe reality.
compiled_state.title: Snapshot entries are not immutable: every ticket read writes .cache.json inside them
